Subject: Private Offer & Commit Drawdown — ACME / GCP Marketplace

Hi all,

Thanks for taking this on. ACME is ready to move forward with a private offer on GCP Marketplace and wants the purchase to be structured as a committed spend with a monthly drawdown against the committed amount (they prefer drawdown rather than an upfront prepaid model). Attached is our current pricing draft and the deal summary we shared with ACME during procurement.

High-level asks:
- GCP: confirm that a private offer can be configured to support a monthly drawdown against a committed/yearly contract and how that maps to the private offer SKU.
- ACME procurement: confirm preferred start date (they mentioned 4/1), billing contact for contract execution, and whether they need invoice-level breakouts for internal chargebacks.
- Internal: Dev/Marissa — please confirm technical SKU mapping and any listing requirements we need to surface in the private offer.

Attachments: pricing-draft-v2.xlsx (pricing + proposed commit tiers)

If we can get confirmation from GCP on the drawdown mechanics we can put the DocuSign in motion and have finance prepare the ACME-specific commitment schedule.

Thanks,
Sergio

sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: Private Offer & Commit Drawdown — ACME / GCP Marketplace

Thanks for the note, Sergio — happy to help. A couple quick clarifying questions so we can scope the private offer properly: 

1) Commit drawdown model: we support private offers with a committed spend that can be consumed via monthly invoices. Typically the private offer is created with a SKU mapping and billing terms; the committed amount is tracked and we invoice monthly against usage until the commit is consumed. Is ACME expecting fixed monthly drawdowns (e.g., equal monthly amortization) or true consumption-based drawdown from the commit pool?

2) Term and rollover: confirm whether unused commit dollars should roll over to the next month or expire. That affects how we set the contract term in our system.

3) Listing assets: we need the legal entity name that will appear in the offer, a short descriptor for the SKU, and the landing page link. Also confirm whether CloudBridge (their reseller) should be added as a reseller/partner to the private offer.

If you can reply with those details we can draft the private offer and share the internal GCP private-offer id for signatory reference.

Best,
Priya — GCP Marketplace PM

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer & Commit Drawdown — ACME / GCP Marketplace

Quick internal note before we loop back to GCP/ACME:

- Technical SKU mapping: recommend we create two SKUs in the private offer: 
  * redwood-inference-hosted-std (on-demand token-based billing for non-committed usage)
  * redwood-inference-commit-100k (commit SKU that maps to the committed monthly drawdown pool)

- Drawdown behavior: GCP's model typically supports either amortized monthly drawdowns OR a pool model where usage deducts from the commit balance. For ACME's use case (bursty batch + low-latency interactive), the "pool" model is better — they get the committed credit and any overage is billed separately. We should document both options in the offer.

- Listing requirements: listing will need a short product description, a small thumbnail, and a minimum of one support contact. I've attached a quick flow diagram (gcp-offer-flow-diagram.png) showing where commit->drawdown happens and how usage feeds into billing.

Caveats: GCP private offers can take 5-10 business days for processing once created; Marketplace listing metadata and legal review can add time. If ACME needs a specific start date (4/1), we should kick this today.

-- Dev

Hi Lena / ACME team — copying finance to make this easy.

Short answers and our proposed contract language: 
- Term & start: 12 months starting 2026-04-01 — confirmed.
- Rollover: per ACME request, unused committed dollars will expire at the end of each month. We'll mark the contract as "no rollover".
- Drawdown: Redwood will set the billing to produce a consolidated monthly invoice. GCP will apply monthly drawdowns against the committed pool; any usage beyond the remaining commit will be invoiced as overage at the agreed overage rates.
- Early termination: if ACME terminates earlier than the 12-month term, we propose a pro-rata credit for unused committed months after validating usage. We can scope exact early termination terms in DocuSign.

I've attached the commitment schedule that maps the yearly commit to monthly drawdowns and the invoicing cadence: RA-ACME-commit-schedule.xlsx

DocuSign: I'll hand off the finalized schedule to legal/ops once GCP confirms the private-offer id. Can you confirm the billing contact? If you prefer we can send to finance@acme-corp.com or the procurement address above.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
